title: API token pricing scenarios and savings playbook
content:
OVERVIEW:
Working spreadsheet + playbook notes for modeling Hosted API unit economics by model and region. Goal: produce succinct pricing levers and recommended MVP changes that recover margin delta if COGS moves +20% (hardware/spot costs) and demonstrate 3 concrete levers that product + infra can implement within 90 days.

QUICK SUMMARY / DECISION POINTS (top lines):
- Baseline: current list pricing assumed $0.06 per 1k tokens for text-gen (example tier).
- Observed weighted COGS (baseline mix) across models: US: $0.0097 / 1k tokens, EU: $0.0116 / 1k, APAC: $0.0142 / 1k.
- Baseline gross margin (list price - COGS)/list price: US ~83.8%, EU ~80.7%, APAC ~76.3%.
- If model mix shifts to larger-context heavy (more completion tokens), unit COGS increases ~+18–25% depending on model and KV cache hit-rate.
- Recommended quick levers: (1) aggressive client-side / server-side batching tuned per-route, (2) default small prompt-caching for repeated system prompts, (3) new per-region price bands + optional committed discount.

ASSUMPTIONS (editable sheet cells):
- Token definitions: prompt tokens vs completion tokens (cost asymmetry assumed: completion tokens are 1.0x baseline compute; prompt tokens delivery counted but often cached).
- Average sequence lengths by workload: search: 80 prompt / 20 completion; chat: 60/120; summarization: 400/1200.
- Model fleet mix (weighted qps baseline): small models (7–13B) = 42%, medium (30–33B) = 38%, large (65–70B+) = 20%.
- Hardware price assumptions (effective amortized cost incl infra, SW, ops): GPU-hour effective = $2.10 (US), $2.50 (EU), $3.10 (APAC) after pooling/spot vs on-demand blends.
- Perf assumptions: tokens/sec per GPU (inference): 1200 for 7B, 420 for 33B, 190 for 70B (avg; depends on quantization).
- Quantization impact: fp16 -> int8 approx x2 throughput, int4 experimental ~x3 in some models; stability trade-offs noted.

SENSITIVITY SCENARIOS (calculated columns):
- Scenario A (baseline): mix as above.
- Scenario B (completion-heavy): completion token volume +40% -> aggregate COGS +14% -> margin compresses by ~4–6 percentage points depending on region.
- Scenario C (hardware cost shock +20%): COGS rises proportionally; in APAC margin becomes <70% for mid/large models.
- Scenario D (batching enabled wide): effective tokens/sec improves 30% -> per-token COGS down 18–22% for latency-tolerant routes.

RECOMMENDATIONS (triaged: quick / mid / longer):
- Quick (0–30d):
  1) Route-level default batching: enable continuous batching for endpoints where P95 latency SLA can be relaxed; expected savings 12–20% on these routes. TODO: add route list (internal).
  2) Prompt caching for system prompts / starter templates: small cache expected to reduce prompt-token load 8–12% for chat apps with repeated templates.
  3) Introduce regional price bands (US / EU / APAC) and optional commit-level discounts to preserve margin for Dedicated customers while keeping hosted list public.
- Mid (30–90d):
  1) Offer a 'latency-tier' pricing option: low-latency premium vs throughput-optimized discounted route (gives customers clear cost/latency tradeoff).
  2) Quantization profiles: certify int8-opt runs for 30B family for hosted early access; run A/B QA for quality regression.
  3) Auto-fallback routing: when capacity expensive, route to smaller quantized variant with price signal + clear labeling.
- Longer (90–180d):
  1) Spot GPU aggregation pool: test cross-region bursts with contractual constraints.
  2) Per-customer consumption patterns -> ML model to recommend optimal model/region choices (savings estimator).

EXAMPLE CALC (rounded):
- Baseline monthly token volume (hosted API): 25B tokens (mix as baseline).
- Monthly COGS US-only baseline: 25B * (weighted COGS 0.0097 / 1k) = 25,000 * 0.0097 = $242.5k.
- If batching reduces per-token COGS by 18% on 60% of volume: savings = 25,000*0.0097*0.6*0.18 = ~$26k/month.
- If combined with prompt caching (10% reduction on 50% of volume): savings additional ~$12k/month.
- Net quick-win savings estimate (conservative): $30–40k/month (12–16% of baseline hosted COGS).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS: (notes to self)
- How to present regional price differences without triggering channel complaints? (work with GTM legal + finance)
- Customer churn sensitivity: what elasticity do we assume for price tier introduction? Need small user study / core customer interviews.
- Quality regressions from quantization: need gating metrics and rollback playbook.
- Billing system changes: should be small (introduce region field + latency-tier flag); estimate 3 sprint work for billing.

ACTIONS / NEXT STEPS (owner assignments):
- Aisha: finalize region band thresholds and run 6-week forecast with finance (due 2025-03-10).
- Ben: prototype route-level batching config and list 10 candidate endpoints (due 2025-02-28).
- Mariana: set up A/B test framework for quantized 30B runs and define regression tests (due 2025-03-17).

NOTES / REFERENCES:
- See Confluence: /team/optimize/pricing-playbook (linked above) for full model detail workbook.
- Quick internal benchmarks: GDrive folder: /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/benchmarks/2025-q1.csv

ROUGH DRAFT FOOTER:
Working doc. Expect many cell-level changes. This sheet is intentionally conservative in assumptions; final pricing recommendations must go through FIN + Legal. If we decide to offer APAC premium, propose a 10% list uplift instead of discounts to maintain foot-gun safety.
